stem: Vikram wants a whole-number bound for $\sqrt{45}$. He knows $6^{2}=36$ and $7^{2}=49$.

options.text: $\sqrt{45}$ lies between $6$ and $7$ only when $45$ is a perfect square.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Because 36<45<49, the square root lies between 6 and 7; nearby perfect squares bound a non-square without needing it to be square.

teacher.key_rationale: 36<45<49 places √45 between 6 and 7. Halving 45 swaps square root for a different operation. Requiring 45 to be square omits that bounds apply to non-squares.
